title: Geometry of 2D Shapes
summary: Classify triangles and quadrilaterals by their properties, use the angle sums of triangles and quadrilaterals and the exterior angle of a triangle, and recognise congruent and similar figures.

notes.text: Triangles can be classified by their **sides** and by their **angles**. Equal sides are shown on diagrams by the same number of small marks (dashes) on each side.

notes.caption: Types of triangles
rows: All three sides equal; all three angles $60^\circ$
Two sides equal; the angles opposite them (base angles) are equal
No sides equal; no angles equal
One angle equal to $90^\circ$; the side opposite it is the hypotenuse

notes.caption: The interior angles of a triangle add up to 180° (reason: ∠ sum of Δ)

notes.text: You can check this by cutting out a paper triangle, tearing off the three corners and placing them next to each other: they always form a straight line ($180^\circ$).
If one side of a triangle is extended, the angle formed outside the triangle is an **exterior angle**. It equals the **sum of the two interior opposite angles** (reason: ext ∠ of Δ).

notes.title: Worked example 1: angles in triangles
notes.problem:
(a) Two angles of a triangle are $47^\circ$ and $68^\circ$. Find the third angle.
(b) In the diagram above, calculate $x$ in two different ways.
steps: Method 2: $\hat{B}_{\text{interior}} = 180^\circ - 50^\circ - 70^\circ = 60^\circ$ (∠ sum of Δ), so $x = 180^\circ - 60^\circ = 120^\circ$ (∠s on a straight line).

notes.title: Worked example 2: an isosceles triangle
notes.problem: In $\triangle ABC$, $AB = AC$ and $\hat{A} = 40^\circ$. Calculate $\hat{B}$ and $\hat{C}$.

notes.label: Exam tip
notes.text: In geometry, every statement needs a **reason** in brackets, e.g. (∠ sum of Δ) or (∠s opp equal sides). An answer without reasons will not get full marks.
A quadrilateral is a closed shape with four straight sides. Its interior angles add up to $360^\circ$, because a diagonal divides it into two triangles: $2 \times 180^\circ = 360^\circ$.

Properties of quadrilaterals
rows: Both pairs of opposite sides parallel and equal
Bisect each other and are equal
All four sides equal; opposite sides parallel
Bisect each other at $90^\circ$; bisect the angles
All four sides equal; opposite sides parallel
Equal, bisect each other at $90^\circ$, bisect the angles
Exactly one pair of opposite sides parallel
Two pairs of adjacent sides equal
One pair of opposite angles equal
Perpendicular; the long diagonal bisects the short one

notes.label: Remember
notes.text: A square is a special rectangle **and** a special rhombus, and all of these are special parallelograms. So "every square is a rectangle" is true, but "every rectangle is a square" is false.

notes.title: Worked example 3
notes.problem: The angles of a quadrilateral are $x$, $2x$, $x + 30^\circ$ and $90^\circ$. Find $x$ and all the angles.
steps: The angles are $60^\circ$, $120^\circ$, $90^\circ$ and $90^\circ$. Check: they add to $360^\circ$ ✓

notes.text: Figures are **congruent** if they have exactly the **same shape and the same size**. One fits exactly on top of the other. We write $\triangle ABC \equiv \triangle DEF$.

In congruent triangles, all corresponding sides are equal and all corresponding angles are equal. The order of the letters matters: $\triangle ABC \equiv \triangle DEF$ means $A$ matches $D$, $B$ matches $E$ and $C$ matches $F$, so $AB = DE$, $BC = EF$ and $\hat{A} = \hat{D}$. Two triangles are congruent if they match by SSS, SAS, ASA (or AAS) or RHS.
Figures are **similar** if they have the **same shape** but not necessarily the same size. One is an enlargement or reduction of the other. We write $\triangle ABC\ |||\ \triangle DEF$.
In similar triangles, corresponding **angles are equal** and corresponding **sides are in the same ratio** (in proportion).

notes.title: Worked example 4: similar triangles
notes.problem: $\triangle ABC\ |||\ \triangle PQR$ with $AB = 6$, $BC = 8$, $AC = 10$ and $PQ = 9$. Calculate $QR$ and $PR$.
steps: $AB$ corresponds to $PQ$, so the scale factor is $\dfrac{9}{6} = 1{,}5$.

notes.label: Common mistake
notes.text: Congruent means same shape **and** same size; similar means same shape only. All congruent triangles are similar, but similar triangles are not always congruent.

items: Triangles: equilateral, isosceles, scalene (sides); acute, right, obtuse (angles).
Angles of a triangle add to $180^\circ$; an exterior angle equals the sum of the interior opposite angles.
Isosceles triangle: the angles opposite the equal sides are equal.
Angles of a quadrilateral add to $360^\circ$. Know the side, angle and diagonal properties of each special quadrilateral.
Congruent ($\equiv$): same shape and size. Similar ($|||$): same shape, equal angles, sides in proportion.
Give a reason for every statement in a geometry calculation.

questions.prompt: A triangle has sides 5 cm, 5 cm and 8 cm. What type of triangle is it?
questions.explanation: Exactly two sides are equal, so it is isosceles.

questions.prompt: Two angles of a triangle are $47^\circ$ and $68^\circ$. Calculate the third angle, in degrees.

questions.explanation: A rectangle has opposite sides equal and parallel and four right angles. A square has all of these properties (and more), so it is a special rectangle.

questions.prompt: A quadrilateral has four equal sides, and its diagonals bisect each other at right angles but are not equal in length. What is it?
questions.explanation: Four equal sides with perpendicular diagonals: rhombus. A square would also have equal diagonals.

questions.prompt: The two interior opposite angles of an exterior angle of a triangle are $55^\circ$ and $65^\circ$. Calculate the exterior angle, in degrees.
In an isosceles triangle the angle between the two equal sides is $40^\circ$. Calculate the size of one base angle, in degrees.
Three angles of a quadrilateral are $90^\circ$, $110^\circ$ and $75^\circ$. Calculate the fourth angle, in degrees.
Match each quadrilateral with a property that describes it.

pairs.right: Two pairs of adjacent sides are equal
Exactly one pair of parallel sides
Both pairs of opposite sides parallel

questions.explanation: Learn the properties table: sides, angles and diagonals for each quadrilateral.

questions.prompt: Congruent triangles have the same shape and the same size.
questions.explanation: That is the definition of congruent. Similar triangles have the same shape only.

questions.prompt: One acute angle of a right-angled triangle is $35^\circ$. Calculate the other acute angle, in degrees.
What do we call a triangle that has one angle greater than $90^\circ$?
questions.explanation: An angle greater than $90^\circ$ (and less than $180^\circ$) is obtuse, so the triangle is obtuse-angled.

questions.prompt: The angles of a triangle are $x$, $2x$ and $3x$. Calculate $x$ and the size of each angle. What type of triangle is it?
questions.memo:
$x + 2x + 3x = 180^\circ$ (∠ sum of Δ) ✓ (1)
$6x = 180^\circ$, $x = 30^\circ$; angles $30^\circ$, $60^\circ$, $90^\circ$ ✓ (1)
Right-angled (and scalene) triangle ✓ (1)

questions.prompt: In $\triangle ABC$, $AB = AC$ and $\hat{A} = 50^\circ$. $BC$ is extended to $D$. Calculate $\hat{ACD}$, giving reasons.
questions.memo:
$\hat{B} = \hat{ACB}$ (∠s opp equal sides) ✓ (1)
$\hat{B} = \hat{ACB} = \dfrac{180^\circ - 50^\circ}{2} = 65^\circ$ (∠ sum of Δ) ✓ (1)
$\hat{ACD} = 180^\circ - 65^\circ$ (∠s on a str line) ✓ (1)
$= 115^\circ$ ✓ (1)
(Or: $\hat{ACD} = \hat{A} + \hat{B} = 115^\circ$, ext ∠ of Δ)
